semantics.note: The normalization preserves the majority threshold and the funding-withdrawal antecedent. The statement expresses a definite belief, not a probability-qualified prediction.

contract.note: Sector-wide funding withdrawal and business closure are ordinary readings. Cohort and timing ambiguities do not determine the present result because the antecedent is unestablished.

evidence.note: Timely financing data bears on the antecedent. Continuing investment does not contradict the conditional prediction about subsequent failures.
Continuing North American AI financing weighs against the antecedent being met. It does not establish post-withdrawal survival and shares the first report's underlying dataset.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish sector-wide withdrawal of venture financing or subsequent majority failure. No deadline was stated. Continuing funding cannot refute a forecast conditional on funding drying up.

attribution.note: Both the survival prediction and the revenue explanation are Zitron's own assertions.

semantics.note: The survival reading is reasonable, but the normalization weakens exclusive revenue dependency to reliance and adds an enterprise restriction. Forecast describes the survival component; the revenue clause is a separate present-tense causal assertion.

contract.note: The business-failure reading and exclusive-dependency test are reasonable. Restricting the present-tense revenue assertion to January–March 2026 imports a period the speaker did not supply. This does not determine the unresolved result.

evidence.note: This timely company filing supplies relevant background, not independent verification. Nine-month customer concentration establishes neither the selected quarter's funding dependency nor either company's ultimate failure.

reviews.rationale: No terminal business-failure event settles the undated forecast. The filing does not trace customer funding or distinguish experimental from production spending, so the revenue assertion is also unresolved. The normalization and selected revenue period need correction.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both thresholds. The qualification about projects ever operating includes unfinished projects; it does not make operating commencement a necessary antecedent.

contract.note: Permanent commercial failure and project-level recovery are reasonable readings. The contract appropriately requires consistent accounting. Missing qualifying outcomes prevent resolution regardless of the remaining accounting ambiguities.

evidence.note: The timely report identifies an unfinished project acquired for conversion to AI use. Its earlier bankruptcy, subsequent acquisition and absent recovery accounts do not establish a qualifying permanent failure.
The timely compilation concerns compute-credit distress and lender recovery. It supplies neither an exhaustive project census nor qualifying project costs and recovery.

reviews.rationale: Neither item establishes permanently failed eligible projects totaling $200 billion with recovery below 25%. There is also no complete terminal accounting that excludes that outcome. No deadline or qualifying early-resolution event is established.

attribution.note: Zitron makes and endorses the financial assertions and circular-financing characterization.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the amounts, counterparties and payment window. These are assertions about existing investments and agreements; the future payment schedule does not make them forecasts.

contract.note: Separating commitments, completed payments and investment rights is fair, as is excluding the unmeasured historical superlative. The packet's missing transaction reconciliation and closed payment schedule prevent resolution without choosing a disputed interpretation.

evidence.note: The company filing supports the $30 billion cloud-commitment amount. Its final payment bucket is open-ended, so it neither establishes the six-year endpoint nor proves material payments fall beyond it.

OpenAI's company disclosure supports announced NVIDIA investment at the claimed scale and reciprocal infrastructure ties. It does not establish completed cash payments or the aggregate cloud-payment schedule.

NVIDIA's disclosure establishes an IREN partnership and conditional investment rights. An optional right does not establish an investment payment or binding funding commitment, but does not prove no other investment occurred.

reviews.rationale: Company disclosures support the cloud-commitment amount and investment scale. The packet does not reconcile investment status across all four counterparties, establish the full six-year payment window or trace the asserted financing relationships sufficiently to settle the composite claim. These gaps are not demonstrated contradictions.
